questions.q: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
questions.e: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire around 321 BCE with the help of Chanakya. Bindusara was his son and Ashoka his grandson. Samudragupta was a Gupta ruler.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The Quit India Movement was launched in 1942.
II. The Quit India Movement was launched under the leadership of Subhas Chandra Bose.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942 with the call 'Do or Die'. Subhas Bose was not leading it; he was abroad organising the Indian National Army.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The Qutub Minar was built by Shah Jahan.
II. The construction of the Qutub Minar was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Aibak laid the foundation of the Qutub Minar in the early 13th century. Shah Jahan lived about four centuries later and built the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid.

questions.q: The Red Fort in Delhi was built by the Mughal emperor
questions.e: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort (Lal Qila) between 1639 and 1648 when he founded his new capital Shahjahanabad.

questions.q: The Battle of Plassey, which established British political power in Bengal, was fought in
questions.e: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey in 1757. The Battle of Buxar followed in 1764 and the Revolt in 1857.

questions.q: The Dandi March of 1930 was launched by Mahatma Gandhi to break which law?
questions.e: Gandhi marched from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi and made salt on the coast, defying the British salt monopoly and starting the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. Ashoka fought the Kalinga war.
II. After the war Ashoka adopted Buddhism and gave up conquest by war.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Ashoka's conquest of Kalinga caused huge suffering. This led him to adopt Buddhism and follow dhamma instead of military conquest.

questions.q: Who defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526?
questions.e: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of Delhi, and laid the foundation of Mughal rule in India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.
II. Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee presided over its first session.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Congress was founded in 1885 with A.O. Hume's initiative, and its first session at Bombay was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee.

questions.q: The period of which dynasty is often called the Golden Age of ancient India?
questions.e: The Gupta age saw great progress in art, literature, mathematics and science, so it is called the Golden Age.

questions.q: The French Revolution began in which year?
questions.e: The Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille on 14 July. 1776 is the American Declaration of Independence and 1815 is Waterloo.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The Alai Darwaza was built by Iltutmish.
II. The Alai Darwaza forms part of the Qutub complex in Delhi.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Alai Darwaza was built in 1311 by Alauddin Khalji, not Iltutmish. It is an entrance gateway within the Qutub complex.

questions.q: Which dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate immediately after the Tughlaq dynasty?
questions.e: The order was Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi. Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty after Timur's invasion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. Alauddin Khalji introduced market regulations that fixed the prices of goods.
II. Sher Shah Suri issued a silver coin called the rupiya.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Alauddin Khalji controlled prices of grain and cloth to support a large army. Sher Shah's silver rupiya became the base of later Indian coinage.

questions.q: The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between Akbar's forces and
questions.e: Mewar's Maharana Pratap fought the Mughal army led by Man Singh at Haldighati. Rana Sanga fought Babur at Khanwa in 1527.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764.
II. At Buxar the English defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Buxar (1764) confirmed British power in eastern India. The Treaty of Allahabad followed in 1765, giving the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The Doctrine of Lapse is most closely associated with Lord Dalhousie.
II. The Subsidiary Alliance system was introduced by Lord Cornwallis.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Dalhousie annexed states such as Satara and Jhansi under the Doctrine of Lapse. The Subsidiary Alliance was Lord Wellesley's system, not Cornwallis's.

questions.q: The Harappan site of Lothal, known for its dockyard, is located in the present-day state of
questions.e: Lothal in Gujarat had a dockyard that shows the maritime trade of the Indus Valley people.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
II. Chauri Chaura, where a violent incident occurred in 1922, is in Bihar.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Gandhi withdrew the movement in February 1922 after the violence at Chauri Chaura, which is in Uttar Pradesh. Jallianwala Bagh was in 1919 and was not the cause.

questions.q: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between
questions.e: At Lucknow in 1916 the Congress and the Muslim League agreed on a joint scheme of reforms, and the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.q: The Poona Pact of 1932 settled the question of separate electorates for the Depressed Classes between Mahatma Gandhi and
questions.e: The pact between Gandhi and Ambedkar replaced separate electorates for the Depressed Classes with reserved seats in the general electorate.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The fort of Tughlaqabad in Delhi was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
II. Tughlaqabad was the capital of the Khalji dynasty.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, built Tughlaqabad. The Khaljis had their capital at Siri.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The League of Nations was established after the First World War.
II. The United States became a member of the League of Nations.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The League was set up after the First World War following the Treaty of Versailles, but the US Senate refused to join it.

questions.q: Match the cities of medieval Delhi with their founders.
questions.e: Siri was built by Alauddin Khalji, Jahanpanah by Muhammad bin Tughluq, Ferozabad by Firoz Shah Tughlaq and Dinpanah by Humayun.

questions.q:
Arrange these battles in ascending chronological order.
1. Haldighati
2. Khanwa
3. First Panipat
4. Talikota
questions.e: First Panipat was in 1526, Khanwa 1527, Talikota 1565 and Haldighati 1576.

questions.q: New Delhi was formally inaugurated as the capital of British India in
questions.e: The shift of capital was announced at the 1911 Durbar, but New Delhi, designed by Lutyens and Baker, was formally inaugurated in 1931.

questions.q: The famous Buddhist centre of learning at Nalanda is traditionally credited to the Gupta ruler
questions.e: Kumaragupta I is traditionally credited with founding the Nalanda mahavihara in the 5th century CE.

questions.q: In the Mughal mansabdari system, the 'sawar' rank of a mansabdar indicated the
o: number of cavalrymen he had to maintain
questions.e: Zat fixed personal status and salary, while sawar fixed the number of horsemen the mansabdar had to maintain.

questions.q: The Treaty of Westphalia (1648) brought an end to the
questions.e: The Peace of Westphalia ended the Thirty Years' War in Europe and is often seen as the start of the modern state system.

questions.q: The Jantar Mantar observatory in Delhi was built in 1724 by
questions.e: Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur built the Delhi Jantar Mantar, with large masonry astronomical instruments, in 1724.
